Z. DESCRI2TION OF INCIDENT
On 16 January 1952, two menbers of a balloon project from the Genera) Mills
Aeronautical Research Laboratory and four other civilians observed two unidentt-
fist aerial objects in the vicinity of the balloon they were observing, Tha
balloon was at an altitude of 112,000 ft, and was 110 ft. in dianeter at the
tine of the observation.
The objects were observed twice, once from‘Artesia, New Mexico, an? once
from the Artesia Airport. In the first instance, one round object ap cared
to remain motionless in the vicinity, but apparently higher, than the balloon,
The balloon appearcd to be 14 inches in dianeter and the object 2) inches in
_ Gimeter (ratio 3:5) and the color was a dull white. This observation was
mate by the two General Mills observers.
A short time later the sane two observers and four civilian pilots were
observing the balloon from the Artesia Airport. Two objecis at apparently
extremely high altitude were noticed coming toward the balloon from the
northwest. They circled the balloon, or apparently so. and flew off to the
northeast, The tine of observation wes about 40 seconds. The two objects
were the same color and size as the first object, They were flying side-b;~-
sic:. When the objects appeared to circle the balloon, they disappeared and
the observers assumed they were disc-shaved and had turned on edge to bank.
II, STATUS OF INVESTIGATION
Unfortunately this report was not made until 5 April and did not reach
ATIC until 16 April. Due to this time lapse, no further investigation is
coztemplated, The observers are known to be very reliable and experienced,
